disk-partition.usage: Enter the whole-GB size you want Windows to display (optionally several sizes at once), choose NTFS or FAT32, and get the exact MB value to type into Disk Management, plus a reference table of common sizes.
tips: The size field in Disk Management is in MB: paste the plain number, without commas or units.
Entering 1024×G (e.g. 102400 for 100GB) usually shows about 99.9 GB, because the file system reserves space for metadata.
NTFS rounds up to whole cylinders of 7.84423828125 MB; FAT32 uses 1024×G + 4×(G−1). Do not mix the two.
Windows Disk Management generally formats FAT32 only up to 32GB; use NTFS or exFAT for larger volumes.
GPT/MBR, 4K alignment and different tools can shift the result by a few MB; a 1–2 MB difference after formatting is normal.
Vendor capacity is decimal (1TB ≈ 931GB in the OS); this tool computes the MB needed for a whole-GB display, which is a different thing.

tips: The same text with the same password produces different ciphertext every time — random salt and IV, by design
A lost password cannot be recovered: there is no reset, no backdoor, no copy kept on a server
The password field is plain text because HTML forms have no password input type here; mind who is watching
Ciphertext is fine to paste into chat, but send the password through a different channel

ua-parse.usage: Paste a User-Agent string and get its browser, engine, OS and device broken out. Leave the box empty to parse your own browser. Anything the regex table cannot recognise is reported as unknown and echoed back verbatim - it never guesses a brand from a similar-looking token. The table carries a last-checked date because UA tokens go stale.
tips: An empty input parses this browser's own UA; pasting someone else's UA does not read or overwrite yours
The regex table was last checked on 2026-11-06 - new browsers (Arc, Quark, WeChat XWEB/X5) change their UA tokens roughly every six months
Unrecognised fields stay "unknown" and the original string is shown; no guessing, no brand inference
Windows 10 and 11 both report NT 10.0, and iPadOS 13+ may report itself as macOS - UA alone cannot tell them apart
The whole string is matched in local memory only: no request, no upload, no local storage

mock-data.usage: Pick a data type and a count to generate fake data for tests. Mobile numbers only use allocated Chinese prefixes; ID numbers carry a real GB 11643 (MOD 11-2) check digit and a real region code. Everything is random and clearly marked as test-only. Export as plain lines, CSV or JSON.
tips: Results are labelled "for testing only, not real numbers": ID sequence codes favour the 000/999 ends to lower collision risk, but zero collisions are not guaranteed
Emails use example.com / .net / .org (RFC 2606 reserved domains) so a stray signup form cannot mail a real person
Mobile prefixes come from the allocated ranges checked on 2026-11-06 - empty ranges like 154 / 164 are excluded
The last ID digit follows GB 11643 MOD 11-2 and is verified again right after generation; you can cross-check it with the ID Validator tool
Only province/city/district names and codes are real; street names and house numbers are made up. Postcodes and coordinates are out of scope
Everything is generated in local memory: no request, no upload, no local storage

json-yaml.usage: Convert JSON to YAML or YAML to JSON, with an automatic direction. Uses js-yaml 4.1.0 (MIT) with an explicit DEFAULT_SCHEMA. Anchors, multiple documents and custom !! tags produce Chinese explanations instead of raw parser exceptions.
tips: Multi-document YAML (--- separated) is one document at a time: the tool tells you to split it instead of silently dropping the rest
Anchors &a / aliases *a are expanded into real data, so the same content may appear twice in the JSON result - a notice is shown
Custom tags like !!str are not understood by DEFAULT_SCHEMA; the error tells you to remove the tag or use a plain scalar
Object key order is preserved; YAML comments are lost in conversion because JSON has nowhere to put them
YAML dates such as 2026-01-01 become strings in JSON, not Date objects
The library is only loaded when you click convert (~39 KB / 13 KB gzip) and never forms part of the first screen

ascii-art.usage: Turn English letters and digits into ASCII art with three figlet fonts (Standard / Slant / Small). Long text wraps at the chosen render width and only breaks at spaces, so words are never split. Non-ASCII input (Chinese, emoji) is rejected with a clear message instead of producing boxes.
tips: Long text wraps at the render width and only at spaces (whitespaceBreak), so words stay intact
Width counts rendered characters, not input characters: the same word is narrower in Small than in Standard
Only English / digits / ASCII punctuation are supported; Chinese and emoji are reported, not rendered as squares
All three fonts measure 58.5 KB raw / 9.8 KB gzip, far below the 200 KB per-tool ceiling, so none were cut
The engine and font data load only when you click generate and never form part of the first screen

pinyin-convert.usage: Convert Chinese characters to pinyin: full syllables or initials, with configurable case and separator. English words and digits are kept verbatim. The bundled dictionary gives syllables only - it does not carry tone marks and never guesses a tone. Polyphonic characters use their common reading (Chongqing becomes "zhong qing"), and this policy is stated on the page and in the result.
tips: No tone marks: the data source only has syllables; the same syllable can have four tones, so guessing a default tone would produce random-looking results
Polyphones use the common reading: "Chongqing" becomes zhong qing; fix place names and personal names by hand
English words and digits stay intact as a block instead of being split into H e l l o; separators only go between adjacent Hanzi
Initials + no separator gives the usual abbreviation, e.g. the People's Republic of China -> zhrmghg
The pinyin bundle is built from the in-repo tiny-pinyin dictionary (~15 KB) and only loads when you click convert
Text is converted in local memory only: no request, no upload, no local storage
